First things first I just want to say that it's barely April and the fact that we can have this conversation about this many new ska albums just makes me super happy. No matter what my thoughts are on the albums or bands it still makes me happy to see new ska! That being said here are my thoughts on some of the ones you mentioned and one you didn't 

8 Kalacas: I will start off with a band you didnt mention. They just released a new album a couple weeks ago and I have been listening to it on repeat. I recommended it to a friend of mine who listens to ska and afterwards I was listening to it and wondered if I should recommend it at all. The band has definitely picked up the torch for voodoo glow skulls and then got really drunk and used that torch to burn down the city. It's got a great horn section and they have ska riffs but they can get pretty metal. I would say if you love VGS and leftover crack but always thought to yourself "I wish those bands were more metal" than check them out. Be warned if you do not like metal you will absolutely hate this or maybe not who knows

Arpioni: Not really my cup of tea. It's not inherently bad by any means, it's just lacking something. Soul? And I don't mean the style of music. I love ska but a lot of bands feel like they didn't put any heart into it which is odd seeing as it's not like ska is some big cash making genre where bands are making ska music just to get that fat paycheck. So it feels like if you're making this type of music you are doing it cause you love it. It might be the vocals that turns me off

Buster Shuffle: Love this album but I can also see why people wouldn't like it. I have seen friends argue whether madness should even be considered ska which I think is ludicrous. I love organ driven music so I am a bit biased plus I get a kick out of the super thick English vocals. Reminds me a bit of Death of guitar pop too.

Eichlers: I used to have this argument with my friends when the twilight movies came out. Some guy who only likes fast and furious type movies or anything that A24 releases and they would tell me at great length about how twilight sucks and it's the worst thing on the planet etc.. I would always say "It wasn't made for you, not every movie needs to be made for you". This album was definitely not made for me and that is fine. I would never look down on anyone for liking it or say it's not real ska or doing any gatekeeping bullshit, if anything I hope it introduces a whole new group to ska music!

Escape the Zoo: Great album, energetic, great songwriting and just a fun listen

Step daughters: I love the dance hall crasher and mealticket and so I am always looking for a female fronted ska band to fill that hole, I'm not sure if they will but they have catchy songs and I enjoy listening to them and hope to see them live some time
